review_scope: graphics helper unsafe metadata/mapping/call order and QMP response/deadline boundaries; host-only execution, no hardware claim

findings.boundary: QMP command identity and success shape
findings.before: Missing return, event-as-reply, or bool/float ID could be accepted as success.
findings.after: Exact integer ID, mandatory return xor error, no event in a response; malformed responses rejected.

findings.before: Expired commands were sent, socket send reused an earlier timeout, pipe writes could block without a deadline.
findings.after: Deadline before send, bounded socket timeout and select/PIPE_BUF-limited pipe writes. A real filled pipe is rejected within its deadline in an isolated child.

findings.before: Buffered readline could accept a complete reply after the shared deadline.
findings.after: Incremental read1 with checks around each chunk and reply parse; modeled late read rejected.

source_review: capture is reached only after validate_graphics_header validates retained page plus extension offset; the copied descriptor validates format, bounds and reserved bytes.
pixel_span validates the entire pixel slice, visible row, color high bits and full extent before write_pixels reaches its first volatile store.
map_framebuffer rejects RAM overlap, checks leaf overlap and device pages/physical width/PAT, and readiness is not published on failure.
In current M2 call order map publishes the software-ready flag before CR3 activation, but no pixel writer is called until activation and audit complete. Reuse must preserve this ordering.
static mut metadata/ROW and input initialization rely on one CPU, IF=0, no reentrant graphics caller, and immutable metadata. Atomic flags do not provide an SMP or preemptive ownership protocol.
G0 run resets the real decoder on the 0xff sentinel; included kernel tests verify parity/timeout/AUX classification and the new decoder test verifies prefix/modifier recovery.
open_limits: Host paging/serial stubs always panic and are not successful mappings. MMIO stores, PAT/PTE state, port-I/O timing and physical input are not exercised.
The actual framebuffer ready flag timing and single-CPU/IF=0 assumptions must be redesigned or explicitly preserved before G1/SMP/preemptive reuse.
QMP transport doubles and a real local pipe prove host harness boundaries only; no VM acceptance run was added here.
